stories.title: Clavicular is scheduled to be arraigned on a Massachusetts rape charge
paragraphs: The Associated Press reported that streamer Braden Peters, known online as Clavicular, was set to be arraigned in Massachusetts on a rape charge.
The report describes a scheduled court proceeding; the saved evidence does not establish what happened at the arraignment or the eventual outcome of the case.
The charge is an allegation, not a finding of guilt. AP identifies Peters as a livestreamer associated with the looksmaxxing trend.

scoreNotes.general: A prominent streamer faces a significant new court date, reported by a national news organization.
scoreNotes.heat: The case involves a widely recognized streamer and a serious criminal charge; saved evidence does not establish audience reaction volume.
scoreNotes.time: The scheduled arraignment is the current development, reported October 21 ahead of the October 22 court date.
scoreNotes.ethos: AP reports the arraignment schedule. The saved evidence does not establish its outcome, and a charge is an allegation, not a finding of guilt.

nearMisses.title: Moonlighter studio shifts ReVamp from a public playtest to a private one over copying concerns
nearMisses.reason: This is a documented development, but it is one studio's response to a broader concern already represented by another recently covered indie demo cancellation; the saved evidence does not establish a wider impact or new audience response strong enough for a main story.

scoreNotes.general: A concrete change to an upcoming game's testing plans, with relevance to indie marketing and exposure.
scoreNotes.heat: The decision reflects a serious developer concern, but the saved discussion is limited and the response is studio-specific.
scoreNotes.time: Reporting and a sampled discussion appeared October 19–20, outside the current 24-hour window.
scoreNotes.ethos: PC Gamer reports the studio's reasoning; a Reddit post independently surfaced the move, but the full primary announcement was not opened.

paragraphs: Moonlighter developer Digital Sun moved the planned public Steam playtest for ReVamp to a smaller, private Discord test, according to PC Gamer.

The report says the studio cited fears that public access could make the game easier to copy or reverse-engineer. A sampled r/Games post described the change, but does not measure broader player or developer opinion.

citations.title: Moonlighter studio won't host a public playtest of its next game due to rampant AI-led cloning: 'We know we're not the only developers feeling this way'
ReVamp's previously-announced public Steam playtest is moving to a private Discord playtest due to concerns over the game being reverse-engineered and copied
